title.narrative: Enabling business environment for sustainable enterprises and employment creation

description.narrative:
Lesotho continues to experience high levels of unemployment, informality, inequality, and poverty. GDP growth has gradually worsened over the past decade, from a peak of 6.3 percent in 2012 to 5.6 percent in 2020, resulting in a 12 percent decline in annual GDP growth. Lesotho’s private sector is largely concentrated in two sectors – mining (predominantly diamonds) and textiles/apparel manufacturing – and economic diversification has proven challenging due to a lack of competitiveness. Most of the firms export to the US market under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) as well as to South Africa.
The ILO has partnered with the International Trade Centre (ITC) in collaboration with the World Bank and the Government of Lesotho to boost the Lesotho T&C industry again as an important contributor to the country`s economy, support is needed to increase its competitiveness and productivity while providing decent work to all workers employed in the sector.
